quote: Yeah. What was it that kinda makes you think that?
stewart_read: This is a strong adaptive capture of the interest/motivation verify item (strategy match to interest_question per llm_context_injection.strategy_recognition), but the objection embedded in the customer's answer ('might not be a worthwhile investment') is never inverted later — the rep treats it as a verify probe rather than the entry point for a bill-anchoring flip.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply missed the objection entirely rather than choosing to defer it.
coaching_implication: Credit the rep for adaptive verify-item capture, but note in the 1-on-1 that the same line that surfaced the objection could have been the launch point for the inversion move later in the call.

quote: the cost is so high. I'm like, okay. So if it's gonna cost me about $20,000 and then, it's saving me only a $100 a month, then it's gonna take, it's gonna take a long time for it to pay for itself.
stewart_read: Textbook trigger for the inversion move (cost objection in first 5 minutes) — customer hands the rep a specific $20k/$100-month framework. Rep responds with 'Mhmm... Yeah. No. I see what you're saying,' validating the customer's framing instead of flipping it toward what their current utility bill is already costing them.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be deliberately not contesting math they don't have real numbers for, deferring to the closer's actual proposal — consistent with setter_scope_discipline. This is plausible given the rep's later admission of being 'just a scheduler.'
coaching_implication: Even without exact numbers, the rep could ask what the customer's current bill is (never captured in this call) to set up the inversion without needing invented figures — that's the specific gap, not a failure to have data.

quote: The only incentive actually that was removed was the federal tax credit, which does actually sound like something that you're interested in. So we've been able to get a lot of new incentives such as state incentives, veteran incentives, stuff like that.
stewart_read: Rep handles the incentive-lapse concern by naming replacement incentive categories rather than creating curiosity about the customer's specific numbers/design — a reasonable reassurance but a missed opportunity to redirect toward 'let's see what your actual design shows' framing.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read (accepted): the rep is filling an information gap defensively rather than strategically pulling the customer toward the appointment as the place to see real numbers.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close incentive-reassurance lines with a curiosity hook ('the design will show exactly what applies to you') rather than resting on the reassurance alone.

quote: Yes. And, actually so I'm closing on this house this coming Monday, so it's not mine yet.
stewart_read: Customer is about to become a new homeowner and is already thinking about tree/roof maintenance — a strong signal of long-term tenure intent and active home-improvement mindset, both of which correlate with solar receptivity.
coaching_implication: Flag as a signal worth noting for the closer even though the rep responded reasonably by continuing the roof/garage conversation — the rep did not explicitly reinforce the new-ownership context as a reason-to-act, which is a fair miss but not costly since the appointment was still secured. Note: this inference is reasonable but not backed by a specific schema section — flagged as ungrounded-but-plausible rather than a scored schema gap.

quote: What about Yeah. Do you see on the Google Maps? What about on the garage? Is that surface area that we could use too?
stewart_read: Customer proactively asks about additional roof surface for panels — an unsolicited question about system capacity/siting that signals real engagement, not just compliance.
coaching_implication: Rep handled this well in the moment ('Yeah. You get lots of sun on that garage'), but the manager should note this as a customer-initiated capacity question worth flagging to the closer as evidence of genuine interest depth.

quote: I know some houses can cover a 100% of the offset. Some only do about half.
stewart_read: Rep just stated 'I'm just like a scheduler' and admitted not knowing the answer, then immediately volunteers unverified percentage figures about offset coverage — a direct violation of numeric_discipline (no fabricated/estimated quantitative claims) layered on top of scope creep.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may be using rough ranges to keep the customer engaged rather than stonewalling — but this doesn't hold because the rep had just correctly used the scope-discipline escape hatch one sentence earlier and then abandoned it.
coaching_implication: This is a specific, replayable moment: rep should have stopped at 'I'm just a scheduler, but my specialist will show you exactly what your roof can cover' — the percentage figures should be struck entirely.

quote: if you have any questions or anything, just feel free to shoot me a a text or something. I'll text you your appointment details just so you have that reminder
stewart_read: Call ends with appointment day/time locked (Tuesday at 5) and a text-follow-up promise, but the rep never runs the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or restates the one-hour block / no-driving requirement before hanging up.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read (accepted): this is a procedural omission, not a deliberate choice — the button-up template's handshake and hour-block elements are simply skipped.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close with the explicit fairness check and hour-block statement even when the call is going well — show rate is tied to this mechanic, not just having a date on the calendar.
